correctness.rationale: For every facet sign sigma the membership probability of row i is q_iσ=(1+sum_j σ_j(a_ij^+−a_ij^-))/2. Because collective expectation sum is zero, sum_i q_iσ=r/2, so AM–GM bounds each independent joint facet probability by 2^(-r). Summing 2^d facet probabilities yields min(1,2^(d-r)). For r<=d distinct fair signed coordinate axes always lie on some common facet. For r>=d, one fair law dedicated to each of the d axes plus arbitrary individually antipodally symmetric additional laws attains 2^(d-r). Equality in the summed facet bounds forces q_iσ=1/2 for every i and all sign σ, whence all individual law signs are balanced for each axis. Conditional on independent axes J_i with K distinct chosen axes, compatible signs have probability 2^(K-r). Thus probability=E 2^(K-r), sharp iff K=d almost surely. An axis appears in every positive-probability independent tuple iff at least one row is entirely supported on it; this proves exact optimizer characterization for r>=d. The r=d case forces a permutation of fair axis laws. Independent rational enumeration for 2<=d<=4 and r<=d+2 confirms constructions and nonoptimizer examples; the analytical finite-axis independence argument proves all dimensions.
residual_risks: Equality classification only for r>=d, not r<d; finite d<=4 arithmetic checks do not prove the universal optimization.
